title: Core Collapse
subtitle: Mass Casualty Surge During a Network Outage

brief.userPrompt: A multi-vehicle crash on the interstate sends a surge of patients to the ED while a failed network core switch has taken down the EHR, lab and imaging connections; the hospital triages and tracks patients on paper, opens surge space and decides on diversion, transfers and crisis standards of care.

overview.theme: Surge on downtime, patient identification, crisis standards of care and return to the record
overview.threat: At 16:38 on Friday, March 13, 2026 the core network switch in room A-B02 fails and the failover core in room C-212 cannot carry the clinical networks. The EHR, the laboratory system, PACS and secure messaging are unreachable. Thirty minutes later EMS announces a multi-vehicle crash with a fuel tanker: 14 patients in the first wave, 22 in the second.
overview.operationalImpact: The ED already holds 31 patients and both ICUs are full. Registration, lab, imaging, medication verification and bed management all work from paper while the hospital receives 36 crash patients. Patient identification, blood supply, ventilators, staff endurance and ICU space limit what the hospital can do, and a partly restored EHR threatens to split the record.
overview.targetAudience: Administrator on Call (Incident Commander), Director of IT (Infrastructure Branch), Chief Nursing Officer (Operations Section Chief), ED Medical Director (Medical Care Branch), Public Information Officer (PIO)
overview.location: Ottawa River Regional Medical Center, Toledo, Lucas County, Ohio

objectives.name: Surge on Downtime
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to accept and treat a mass casualty incident with the EHR, laboratory and imaging interfaces unavailable, using Code Triage and the Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex.

objectives.name: Patient Identification and Tracking
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to track patients on paper with trauma and DT- numbers without creating duplicate or crossed identities.

objectives.name: Capacity and Crisis Standards
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to open surge space, move patients, request transfers and decide on crisis standards of care with physician leadership.

objectives.name: Return to the Record
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to decide when a partly restored system may be used and how the paper record is reconciled.

roles.name: Administrator on Call (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Helen Marchetti, Chief Operating Officer. Activates the HICS structure, decides diversion, downtime level and public positions, and owns the Incident Action Plan.
standingOrders: Decide with the Chief Medical Officer when a technical isolation changes how patients are cared for.
Keep the Policy Group (CEO, CMO, CNO, General Counsel) informed within 30 minutes of a Cyber 1 event.

roles.name: Director of IT (Infrastructure Branch)
roles.description: Raymond Okafor. Restores the network core and the clinical systems, rules a cyberattack in or out with the Information Security Officer, and gives realistic restore times.
standingOrders: Tell the HCC the time you will report next, even when you have no news.
Do not bring a partly restored system back into clinical use without telling the CNO what it will and will not show.

roles.name: Chief Nursing Officer (Operations Section Chief)
roles.description: Carol Beckett. Runs patient care while systems are down: downtime procedures, medication safety, staffing and unit census.
standingOrders: Patient safety first: two-person checks replace barcode scanning for high-alert drugs and blood.
Units report census, acuity and open beds at the top of every hour at Level 1.

roles.name: ED Medical Director (Medical Care Branch)
roles.description: Dr. Elaine Whitfield. Runs triage and treatment in the ED and decides, with the AOC, diversion, expectant categories and which patients go to which surge space.
standingOrders: Keep the ED moving: discharge and move admitted patients out of the ED to make room.
Triage decisions in a crisis-standards situation are made by a physician, never a registration clerk.

roles.name: Public Information Officer (PIO)
roles.description: Kevin Dunmore. Releases information only from facts cleared by the Information Security Officer and the Chief Privacy Officer.
standingOrders: Never say patient data was not accessed unless the Chief Privacy Officer has cleared the words.
Keep a media log; patient-specific information is released only as the Chief Privacy Officer allows.

phases.title: Dark Network
phases.goal: Run the ED and the units on downtime while IT works the switch, and decide to accept a mass casualty incident with the clinical systems down.
beats: The core switch in room A-B02 fails at 16:38 and failover to room C-212 does not take.
EMS reports a multi-vehicle crash with a fuel tanker; 14 patients are on the way, six critical.
Blood bank cannot see antibody history and asks for emergency release.

phases.title: First Wave
phases.goal: Receive 14 patients on paper, keep patient identification safe, open operating rooms and handle the crowd and the rumors.
beats: Two arrivals get two different wristband numbers.
The OR needs three more rooms and instruments with no PACS for intra-operative imaging.
A second wave of 22 is announced when the ICU has no beds.

phases.title: Capacity
phases.goal: Decide transfers, the use of surge space, staff relief and expectant triage, and talk to families and the press.
beats: A neighboring hospital can take six ICU transfers but needs a record that the hospital cannot print.
Staff are at 12 hours and the day shift cannot go home.
The CMO asks the AOC to approve crisis standards for three expectant patients.

phases.title: Network Back, Record in Doubt
phases.goal: Decide when and how to bring a partly restored EHR back, reconcile paper and system, and set the demobilization criteria.
beats: A restored core brings the EHR back read-only while registration remains down.
The lab backlog produces duplicate and conflicting results.
The exercise ends with the hospital still at Level 1 for the night and the replacement switch not yet installed.

msel.event: STARTEX: It is 16:45 on Friday, March 13, 2026 at Ottawa River Regional Medical Center. At 16:38 the core network switch in room A-B02 failed. Failover to the second core in room C-212 did not take, and the EHR, the laboratory system, PACS and secure messaging are unreachable from most clinical networks. The telephones work. The IT on-call and the Nursing Supervisor declared downtime at 16:41. The ED holds 31 patients, both ICUs are full, and OR 1 and OR 2 each have a case in progress. The vendor says four hours for a replacement. Nothing yet suggests anything other than a hardware failure.
msel.expectedAction: Players read the situation and set the first priorities. No decision is forced yet.

msel.event: Helpdesk Ticket INC-26-03-0577, priority 1: "Core stack member 2 in A-B02 is in a boot loop after a power fault on the stack link. The C-212 core did not take over because its configuration is from February 27 and does not include the clinical VLANs added in change CHG-1184 on March 4. I can load the March 10 backup config onto C-212, which would bring the clinical VLANs up but not the PACS and device VLANs, in about 45 minutes. Replacement hardware from the vendor is four hours away."
msel.expectedAction: The Director of IT chooses the partial restore on C-212 now (clinical VLANs first) and orders the replacement chassis in parallel. The Information Security Officer is told to verify that the failure has no malicious cause (logs on both cores) and rules it out in writing before the HCC treats it as plain hardware. The Director of IT gives the HCC a time to report next.

msel.event: Phone Call: "Marcus Bell, ED charge. I have two chest-pain patients waiting for a troponin, a stroke alert that needs a CT read, and a belly pain with a possible appendicitis who needs imaging. Nothing goes out and nothing comes back. We are walking specimens to the lab and films to Imaging. I have 31 patients and one runner. Tell me what you want me to do."
msel.expectedAction: The ED Medical Director and the CNO use the downtime process: point-of-care testing for troponin and glucose where available, a paper tracking board, runners from Environmental Services and Security, CT reads by the radiologist at the console, and a stroke alert pathway that does not wait for the PACS. The CNO assigns three more runners (Downtime Annex, Section 5).

msel.event: Radio Call: "Lucas County EMS to Ottawa River. Multi-vehicle crash on the interstate with a fuel tanker, fire on scene. First wave: 14 patients, six critical, ETA 12 minutes. More are expected. You are our trauma center. Are you accepting?"
msel.expectedAction: The AOC and the ED Medical Director accept: Code Triage is called, a Level 1 activation is declared, the Triage Officer moves to the ambulance bay, the Decontamination and Isolation Suite is made ready for a possible fuel exposure, and EMS is told the hospital is accepting trauma but is on downtime with no PACS or lab interfaces. Non-MCI ambulance diversion is considered separately (Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex, Section 3 and Annex A).

msel.event: PA Announcement: "Code Triage, Code Triage. Mass casualty incident. All department managers report to the Hospital Command Center. Surgical Pavilion, Imaging and Laboratory: report your capacity to the HCC. All staff: downtime procedures are in effect. Code Triage, Code Triage."
msel.expectedAction: The HCC fills in under the HICS structure. The AOC convenes the first HCC meeting within 30 minutes (EOP Section 4) and the Liaison Officer opens a line to Lucas County EMS and the Lucas County EMA. The CNO calls in staff through the call-in tree.

msel.event: Phone Call: "Blood Bank. I have six critical patients coming and no way to see antibody history because the lab system is off the network. I have 14 units of O-negative and 22 of O-positive. I need the physician to authorize emergency release and I need a second person to check every unit at the bedside. I will also ask the regional blood center for more."
msel.expectedAction: The ED Medical Director and the Blood Bank follow the emergency-release process: physician signature, second-person check, paper administration record, O-positive for men and O-negative kept for women of childbearing age and unknown types. Blood Bank calls the regional blood center for O-negative and plasma and the CNO assigns a second checker to the ED resuscitation bays.

msel.event: TIME_JUMP: It is now 17:45. The first 14 patients have arrived; six are critical. C-212 now carries the clinical networks, so the EHR can be reached read-only from some computers, but registration, PACS and secure messaging are still down. Tracking is on the paper board with trauma numbers T-1 to T-14.
msel.expectedAction: Players update their picture and set the next operational period objectives.

msel.event: Field Report (Registration to HCC): "Two patients have two numbers. A man brought in as T-6 was registered at the desk as DT-004112 by a clerk who had not been told about the trauma numbers, and a woman is T-9 on the board and DT-004118 on her band. I also have a crash victim with no ID who may be the same person as a patient registered by his brother. I have 6 clerks and 3 blocks of DT numbers."
msel.expectedAction: The CNO and the ED Medical Director stop the use of two series at the bedside: trauma patients keep the T- number, and Registration cross-references it to a DT- number on the paper tracking board once, under one supervisor. Every wristband and specimen label is checked by two people (Downtime Annex, Section 3 and Section 5). The CPO is told because crossed identities can become a privacy event.

msel.from: Surgical Pavilion Charge Nurse Priya Nair
msel.event: Phone Call: "Priya in the Surgical Pavilion. OR 1 and OR 2 are closing. I have three trauma laparotomies and an orthopedic case waiting; ORs 3, 4 and 5 are ready but I have staff for four rooms and the sterile processing department is behind. We have no PACS for intra-operative imaging and the hybrid rooms 11 and 12 cannot show prior studies. Do I cancel the evening elective list and recall staff?"
msel.expectedAction: The Chief Medical Officer and the AOC cancel all elective cases, recall off-duty OR staff, and open ORs 3 to 5 for trauma. The CNO moves instruments priority in Sterile Processing to trauma sets. Imaging uses portable films and the console for intra-operative images; hybrid rooms stay available for vascular cases. The AOC tells the Surgical Pavilion when it can expect imaging support.

msel.event: Radio Call: "Security to HCC. About 90 family members and friends are in the Tower B lobby and the ED waiting room, and a Channel 11 truck is at the main entrance. Some families are trying to walk through the ambulance bay. I need a reunification room away from the ED and a decision on who talks to the press."
msel.expectedAction: The AOC activates the family reunification center in the Tower A lobby (Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex, Section 3), staffed by Social Work and Spiritual Care, with Security controlling the ambulance bay and two public entrances. The PIO sets a media position away from patient areas. Patient information goes only to verified family and only as the CPO allows.

msel.event: Facebook Post (Group: Toledo Scanner Watch): "Tanker on fire and Ottawa River is on lockdown with their computers down. Do NOT go to Ottawa River, take people to a different hospital. Heard they are turning people away." 340 reactions, 96 comments.
msel.expectedAction: The PIO releases a short statement cleared by the AOC and the ED Medical Director: the Emergency Department is open and treating emergencies; the hospital is handling a technology disruption and a mass casualty incident; non-urgent patients should call first or use urgent care. The PIO also tells Lucas County EMS and the EMA so that official channels say the same.

msel.event: Email Forward (from the Director of IT): "C-212 is carrying the clinical VLANs. The LIS came back at 18:20 but the interface engine ORRMC-INT01 is stuck, so results flow one way. The EHR is up read-only on 60 computers. If we let the units chart in the EHR now, the 4-5 hours of paper will need to be re-keyed and the record will be split across two systems with a system that may drop again. I recommend we stay on paper for orders and medications and use the EHR to read."
msel.expectedAction: The AOC decides with the CMIO, the CNO and the Director of IT: the EHR is used only to read until the interface engine is stable and the downtime packet is reconciled; paper stays the record for orders and medications; the Director of IT tells the units exactly what the screens will and will not show. The decision and the reason go in the HCC log.

msel.event: Radio Call: "EMS to Ottawa River. Second wave: 22 patients across three ambulances and two buses, eight critical, ETA 15 minutes. Is there any chance you divert some to another hospital? We have four others on standby."
msel.expectedAction: The AOC and the ED Medical Director use the surge levels in the annex: ICU is full, so PACU becomes an ICU overflow, the Pavilion C treatment areas open for minor injuries, and EMS is asked to send the most severe patients here and the minor injuries to the other hospitals. The Liaison Officer asks the coalition for ICU transfers out. The decision is recorded as Surge Level B moving to C.

msel.event: TIME_JUMP: It is now 18:45. 36 crash patients have arrived in total; 11 are critical and 4 are in the OR. The PACU holds six ICU overflow patients. The ED holds 64 patients, and ICU 3 North and ICU 3 South have no free beds. The replacement switch is on a courier's truck, ETA 21:30.
msel.expectedAction: Players move to capacity problems that come with a large surge.

msel.event: Phone Call: "Transfer center at a neighboring hospital. We can take six of your ICU patients. We need a summary for each: diagnosis, medications, allergies and last labs. We cannot see your chart. How will you send it, and who will give the physician-to-physician report?"
msel.expectedAction: The CNO and the ED Medical Director use the printed BCA-VIEW01 report (last refreshed 16:30) plus the paper record for each patient and give a physician-to-physician report; disclosure to the receiving hospital is allowed for treatment under HIPAA, and the CPO is informed. The Patient Movement Log records time, destination, transport and receiving contact (Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex, Section 5).

msel.event: Field Report (Pharmacy to HCC): "Opioid pulls from the override cabinets in the ED have tripled. Orders on paper are being re-written by the covering resident, and I found three antibiotics ordered twice for the same open-fracture patient. I need pharmacists in the ED and PACU, a count of every override pull by 20:00, and a decision on the antibiotic orders."
msel.expectedAction: The CNO places a pharmacist in the ED and PACU, requires the paper order sheet to be the only order source in the ED, counts override pulls on the half hour, and has the duplicates cancelled by the physician and the pharmacist. The CMO reminds residents that verbal orders are read back and signed within 24 hours.

msel.event: Status Board (HCC capacity board, 19:10): ED 64 of 90 spaces; ICU 3 North 16/16, ICU 3 South 16/16, PACU overflow 6/10; ORs 1-5 in use, 6-8 staffed; blood bank O-neg 4 units; ventilators 31 of 38 in use; staffed beds 340, census 351; EHR read-only; PACS down; secure messaging down; replacement switch ETA 21:30.
msel.expectedAction: The AOC reads the board and acts on two numbers: ventilators (31 of 38) and O-negative blood (4 units) are the next shortages. The AOC asks the coalition for ventilators and the regional blood center for a courier and sets the next capacity report for 19:40.

msel.event: Media Inquiry Phone Slip: "Laura Chen, Channel 11. How many victims has Ottawa River received and how many are dead? We have a family saying their relative is critical and nobody will tell them anything. Is it true the hospital computers are down? We want to report names."
msel.expectedAction: The PIO gives general numbers and general condition only as cleared by the AOC and the Chief Privacy Officer, no names (patient-specific information is released only as the CPO allows), confirms that the hospital is treating the injured while handling a technology disruption, and points families to the reunification center. Fatality numbers come from the county coroner or EMS, not from the hospital.

msel.event: Phone Call: "Sana Qureshi, supervisor. About 140 nurses have been here 12 hours or more and many want to leave but cannot because the day shift is still covering. We have 30 staff from call-ins and nobody for the PACU overflow. Meals are not arranged and two nurses need childcare. What can I authorize?"
msel.expectedAction: The CNO and Human Resources open the staff care unit (meals, rest, childcare), rotate staff out in four-hour blocks, approve mandatory overtime limits, bring in credentialed volunteers from the registry for non-clinical tasks only, and ask the coalition for travel nurses. The AOC approves overtime and the PACU overflow gets nurses from the Surgical Pavilion.

msel.from: Chief Medical Officer Dr. Samuel Obuya
msel.event: Memo: "To the AOC. Of the 22 arrivals in the second wave, three have injuries that, with our current resources, have a very low chance of survival: two with massive head injuries and one with 70 percent burns. We are in surge Level C. I propose to classify them expectant (comfort care) so that the OR, blood and ventilators go to patients who can be saved. I need your approval and I want an ethics consult in the room."
msel.expectedAction: The AOC authorizes crisis standards of care for the ED with the CMO and the ED Medical Director: the decision is a physician decision with a second physician and the ethics service, documented on the paper triage tag; families are told by a physician and Spiritual Care; the decision is reviewed hourly as resources change (Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex, Section 2).

msel.event: TIME_JUMP: It is now 19:45. Six ICU patients have been transferred out and the PACU overflow is down to three. Three expectant patients are receiving comfort care with their families. The hospital is at 351 patients, the ED at 58. The replacement switch is in the building and the installation team will start at 21:30.
msel.expectedAction: Players move to the return to the record.

msel.event: Field Report (Laboratory to HCC): "The LIS is back but the interface engine is not. I have 140 specimens waiting, results typed from the analyzers by hand, and I found a potassium of 6.8 for a patient whose paper result says 4.2. One of the two is a transcription error and the patient is on 4 West. I need to tell the unit which one to trust."
msel.expectedAction: The CNO has the lab repeat the potassium stat, hold both values until the repeat is back, and place a nurse at the bedside; the lab manager makes a second person check all hand-typed critical results against the analyzer printout. The Director of IT is told that the lab backlog depends on the interface engine and gives the HCC a restore time.

msel.event: Phone Call: "Lucas County EMA. The Ohio Department of Health asked for a status from every hospital that took crash patients. Please give me: patients received, critical count, beds open, diversion status, and what resources you need overnight. I also need to know if you can take the second-wave patients still at the scene."
msel.expectedAction: The AOC (or the Liaison Officer) gives the numbers, states that the hospital is on Level 1 for the night, asks for the resources it needs (ICU transfers out, ventilators, blood, nurses), and says whether the hospital will take more patients. The AOC does not promise capacity it cannot staff.

msel.event: Email Forward (from the Chief Privacy Officer): "Three things for the log. We shared patient summaries with a neighboring hospital for treatment, which is permitted. Two registration clerks used both numbers for the same patient, so there are two records for one person and a risk that results post to the wrong one. A reporter was able to see a paper tracking board through the ED door for an hour. I want the board covered and the reconciliation list started."
msel.expectedAction: The AOC has the board moved out of public sight, and the CPO starts the privacy log: disclosures for treatment, the crossed identity pair and the exposed board. The CPO tells the PIO that nothing about a patient is said to media. The HIM Director starts a list of DT- and T- numbers to merge in the record.

msel.event: Sitrep 5, 20:20: "Census 349. ED 52. ICU full. PACU overflow 3. Five ORs in use. EHR read-only; registration and PACS down. Replacement switch to be installed at 21:30, expected up by 23:30. The AOC must set the operational plan for the night, the criteria for stepping down from Level 1, and who decides when the EHR is used for charting."
msel.expectedAction: The AOC sets the night operational period: stay at Level 1 until the new switch is in and tested; the EHR returns for charting only after the Director of IT reports a stable interface engine and the CMIO and CNO agree on a reconciliation plan; the stepdown criteria are no surge patients in the ED holding, ICU capacity restored and the network stable for two hours; the next sitrep is at 22:30.

msel.event: ENDEX: It is 20:45. The hospital is at Level 1 for the night. The replacement switch is not yet installed, the EHR is read-only, registration and PACS are still down and the paper record is the only record. Six patients were transferred out and three expectant patients are receiving comfort care. The reconciliation of two identity series and the lab backlog have not begun.
msel.expectedAction: Move to the hot wash.

metrics.name: Operational Coordination
metrics.fail: Ops roles failed to synchronize on surge activation: the AOC did not convene the HCC within 30 minutes of I-04, and the CNO did not activate the call-in tree until 10 minutes after I-02, delaying staffing for the ED and surgical teams. The Liaison Officer did not open a line to Lucas County EMA until 1:30, after I-08, missing the opportunity to coordinate patient diversion and resource requests in real time.
metrics.pass: The AOC convened the HCC within 30 minutes of I-04 and activated the call-in tree within 5 minutes of I-02. The Liaison Officer opened a line to Lucas County EMA and the regional healthcare coalition by 1:00, enabling timely coordination of patient diversion and staff requests. The CNO assigned three additional runners per Downtime Annex, Section 5, and the Surgical Pavilion activated ORs 3–5 for trauma after I-07.
metrics.excellence: The AOC convened the HCC within 15 minutes of I-04, activated the call-in tree immediately after I-02, and assigned a dedicated runner to the ED from Facilities to support triage. The Liaison Officer proactively contacted the regional healthcare coalition and Lucas County EMA before I-08, and the CNO deployed a pharmacist to the ED and PACU before I-13, anticipating medication errors. The AOC established a 15-minute reporting cycle for all sections by 1:00.

metrics.name: Technical Competence
metrics.fail: The Director of IT delayed the partial restore of C-212 despite having the March 10 backup config available, and did not verify the failure's non-malicious nature before proceeding. The EHR was used for charting after I-10 without a stable interface engine, creating a split record. The lab's hand-typed potassium result was accepted without a repeat, risking a critical medication error.
metrics.pass: The Director of IT chose to load the March 10 backup config onto C-212 to restore clinical VLANs within 10 minutes of I-01, and verified the failure was non-malicious via logs from both cores. The EHR was used only for read-only access after I-10, and the lab repeated the potassium stat and held both values until the result was confirmed. The Director of IT reported a stable interface engine by 22:30.
metrics.excellence: The Director of IT immediately loaded the March 10 backup config onto C-212 and verified the failure was non-malicious via logs from both cores within 5 minutes of I-01. The EHR was used only for read-only access after I-10, and the lab repeated the potassium stat and held both values until the result was confirmed. The Director of IT provided a real-time status update to the HCC every 15 minutes, and the interface engine was restored by 20:00.

metrics.name: Public Communication
metrics.fail: The PIO released a statement to Facebook before confirming the hospital was open for emergencies, and did not consult the AOC or EDMD first. The PIO allowed a reporter to see the paper tracking board through the ED door for an hour, violating privacy policy. The AOC did not authorize a media statement until 2:35, after I-15.
metrics.pass: The PIO released a statement cleared by the AOC and EDMD after I-09, stating the ED was open and treating emergencies. The PIO told Lucas County EMS and the EMA to disseminate the same message. The paper tracking board was covered after I-20, and the CPO was notified of the exposure. The AOC approved the media statement within 10 minutes of I-15.
metrics.excellence: The PIO released a statement within 5 minutes of I-09, cleared by the AOC and EDMD, and directed the EMA and Lucas County EMS to echo the message. The paper tracking board was covered immediately after I-20, and the CPO was notified within 2 minutes. The PIO issued a holding statement for a potential media inquiry every 30 minutes, and the AOC approved a media briefing at 21:00.

metrics.name: Use of Doctrine
metrics.fail: The AOC did not cite any EOP section when activating Code Triage or declaring a Level 1 activation. The CNO did not reference Downtime Annex, Section 5 when assigning runners. The CMO did not cite Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex, Section 2 when authorizing crisis standards of care. The CPO did not reference C3 or C4 when reporting privacy violations.
metrics.pass: The AOC cited EOP Section 4 when convening the HCC and Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex, Section 3 when activating the family reunification center. The CNO cited Downtime Annex, Section 5 when assigning runners and C3 for emergency blood release. The CMO cited Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex, Section 2 for crisis standards of care. The CPO cited C3 and C4 for privacy disclosures and exposure.
metrics.excellence: The AOC cited EOP Section 4 and Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex, Section 3 for Code Triage activation and family reunification. The CNO cited Downtime Annex, Section 5 for runner assignment and C3 for emergency blood release. The CMO cited Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex, Section 2 for crisis standards of care and C4 for privacy policy. The CPO cited C3 and C4 for privacy violations and C2 for the after-action report. All decisions were documented in the HCC log with section references.

objectiveCapabilities.why: The objective tests the hospital's ability to maintain critical infrastructure functions—such as EHR, lab, and imaging—during a network outage, and to stabilize operations using alternate systems and procedures, which is the core of Infrastructure Systems.

The objective requires unified coordination across departments (ED, IT, Blood Bank, etc.) under the HICS structure, ensuring that all stakeholders follow a common operational plan, which is the essence of Operational Coordination.

The objective focuses on maintaining accurate patient identification and tracking using paper-based systems when electronic systems fail, which directly relates to the integrity and continuity of infrastructure systems during a disruption.

The objective includes preventing misinformation and ensuring accurate public communication about patient status, which relies on coordinated, reliable, and timely information release to the public and families, a key function of Public Information and Warning.

The objective tests the ability to expand capacity through surge space activation, patient movement, and crisis standards of care, all of which depend on the hospital’s ability to manage and stabilize its infrastructure systems under extreme stress.

The objective requires the use of pre-established plans (e.g., Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex, Section 2) to make decisions on crisis standards of care, patient movement, and resource allocation, which is a direct application of the Planning capability.

The objective tests the structured process for returning to electronic record systems after a downtime, including verification of system integrity, reconciliation of paper and electronic records, and controlled resumption of EHR use—core functions of Infrastructure Systems.

The objective includes verifying that the restored environment is safe for clinical use, which requires a formal cybersecurity verification process (e.g., Information Security Officer confirmation), making Cybersecurity a critical component of the return-to-record process.

eegs.target: The hospital maintains continuity of critical infrastructure functions by using paper-based systems, alternate care spaces, and manual processes for orders, medications, lab and imaging, and patient tracking, as directed in the Downtime Annex (Section 5) and Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex (Section 3), ensuring patient care continues during EHR and network outages.

hotwash.methodDescription: Use the 3-Up, 3-Down method by asking each team to share three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the exercise. Go around the room by team, capture responses on a whiteboard, and emphasize that this is a no-blame, learning-focused discussion to surface key insights from the scenario.

questions.text: When did you first stop trusting the EHR or the lab report during the outage, and what evidence led you to make that decision instead of relying on the system?

At the 1:30 Facebook post, you had misinformation spreading while you were still assessing the actual status. What information did you need to decide whether to address the post publicly, and who should have made that call?

At 1:40, you received the IT memo recommending you stay on paper despite partial EHR recovery. What made you decide to keep using paper for orders, and how would a different decision have changed the workflow in the ED and ORs?
When the pharmacist reported duplicate antibiotic orders and tripled opioid pulls, what system or process failed to prevent those errors, and what immediate action could have closed that gap?

When you were deciding whether to classify three patients as expectant at 2:55, what did you trust most—the clinical data, the ethics consult, or the pressure to use limited resources on 'saveable' patients—and how did that shape your decision?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment where all participants are encouraged to explore decisions and their consequences without fear of judgment.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented—no external information or updates are provided beyond the injects.
Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures as described in the referenced documents, and roles act within their assigned authorities.
artificialities: Time jumps between modules simulate the passage of hours; actual time does not pass in real time.
The SimCell operates all external stakeholders, including EMS, neighboring hospitals, media, and regional agencies, and provides injects via pre-scripted messages.
Systems such as the EHR, LIS, PACS, and interface engine are named and described in the plans but are not physically accessed or manipulated during the exercise.
Injects are delivered via paper and screen, not through actual network or system failures.
The exercise does not require actual coordination with off-site facilities or vendors; all responses are simulated through role-based discussion.

modules.narrativeMd: It is 16:45. The core network switch in room A-B02 has failed, and the backup core in C-212 did not take over due to outdated configuration. The EHR, laboratory, imaging, and secure messaging systems are unreachable across most of the clinical network. Telephones remain functional. The IT on-call and Nursing Supervisor have declared a downtime event. The ED holds 31 patients, both ICUs are full, and two operating rooms are in use. The vendor estimates four hours for a replacement switch. At 16:50, a network engineer reports that C-212’s configuration is from February 27 and lacks the March 4 VLAN updates. Loading the March 10 backup would restore clinical VLANs but not PACS or device networks. The ED charge nurse reports that critical tests are delayed and no results or orders can be sent. At 17:05, Lucas County EMS announces a multi-vehicle crash with a fuel tanker, 14 patients expected, six critical. The hospital is designated as the trauma center. The switchboard operator announces Code Triage and calls all department managers to the Hospital Command Center.
